title: Insurance duty abolished (ACT)
summary: The ACT phased out duty on insurance premiums, previously 10% on general and 5% on life insurance, as part of the tax reform program it began in 2012, and set the rate to nil for all insurance from 1 July 2016. General rates replaced the revenue.

instruments.title: Duties Act 1999 (ACT)
instruments.provisions: insurance duty, set to nil by a determination under s 139 of the Taxation Administration Act 1999

commenced.what: Insurance duty set to nil on all insurance premiums

direction_rationale: Abolishing insurance duty lowers the cost of cover; the ACT replaced the revenue with general rates, an efficient land tax.

verified.notes: The 1 July 2016 date is from the explanatory statement for the ACT duties determination, read in full. The earlier rates and the start of the phase-out in 2012 are from search results (law-firm and trade press summaries); the ACT Revenue Office site refuses automated requests.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 28 October 2026 (phase 4, second tranche, of the productivity framework pivot) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify the description, industries and assessment before use.

assessment.summary: Abolished duty on insurance premiums, replacing the revenue with general rates. People and businesses pay less for cover, as the Henry Review recommended.

marks.reason: Removes a tax that discouraged insurance, replaced by a broad land tax.
